options.description: Asks with plain lines in and lines out rather than a region that redraws, for a screen reader: the question is written once, what is typed is echoed where it is typed, and nothing already written is ever moved or erased.
options.name: accessible

options.description: Whether Escape leaves the prompt to go back a step. Defaults to `false`, where Escape does nothing, as it always has.
options.name: back

options.description: Shows a month grid under the field, with the day the field holds selected. `true` takes the defaults; an object also names the language, the weekday a row starts on and the days to mark. Page Up and Page Down then change the month.
options.name: calendar

options.description: Where the field starts. Defaults to now, truncated to what is shown and pulled into `min` and `max`. One given here is taken as it is, so it can start outside the range -- and Enter on it is then an error rather than a quiet move to the nearest bound.
options.name: initial

options.description: The latest answer, inclusive at the precision shown.
options.name: max

options.description: The earliest answer, inclusive at the precision shown.
options.name: min

options.description: The input router to read keys through. One is built if not given.
options.name: router

options.description: Shows the second too, which implies `time`. Defaults to `false`.
options.name: seconds

options.description: Gives the prompt up when this aborts, the way Ctrl-C does.
options.name: signal

options.description: Where keys come from. Defaults to the terminal's input.
options.name: stdin

options.description: Shows the hour and minute as well. Defaults to `false`: a date.
options.name: time

options.description: Checks the answer. Return a string to reject it with that message, or anything falsy to accept.
options.name: validate
options.type: (value: Date) => string | undefined | false | Promise<string | undefined | false>

options.description: An answer to start from: where the field starts, beating `initial` and taken as it is the same way. One that is not a valid date is dropped rather than refused, leaving `initial` to decide.
options.name: value

registryDescription: A date prompt: year, month and day segments, with min and max
